newsitem.title: UK: UK power mkt liberalisation may be delayed - paper.
newsitem.headline: UK power mkt liberalisation may be delayed - paper.

text.p: Plans for liberalising Britain's electricity supply market by April 1998 may be delayed due to problems with implementing back-up systems in case of computer failure, a British newspaper said on Tuesday.
A report to the electricity industry regulator Offer said two contingency plans being considered might be so time-consuming and complicated they could fail to work on time, the Independent said.
It obtained the information from a leaked report from PA Consulting Group to Offer.

Last week Offer's head, Professor Stephen Littlechild, said the complex process of transferring customers to alternative electricity suppliers might have to be done manually if new computers broke down.
He told Britain's parliament a manual system was part of contingency plans but said there was currently "no reason to change" timetables.
Electricity companies need to set up computer systems to handle both internal changes and complicated interfaces between companies, the supply market and producers.
